utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I was wondering if while we wait I could just announce in respect to the application before the Court for videolink for Shyhrete Dula. The Prosecution has investigators now in Pristina preparing for the upcoming videolink and they have spoken to her and encouraged her. And she has indicated that notwithstanding her issues she is now ready and willing to come here. So in those circumstances we withdraw that application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You don't know how close you were in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I would remind you the affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. Mr. Djurdjic is continuing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For a moment, Mr. Djurdjic, I thought you had completed your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what it appeared to be, but that's not quite what it is. Now the mike is working.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. My microphones are on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, it's all right. Both your and my microphone are on.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, only one of my microphones is on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I don't know if this will interfere with interpretation, but let's try it. Good morning, Mr. Veljkovic.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So let me just remind you to speak slowly so that everything we say is properly interpreted and enters into transcript. Mr. Veljkovic, we finished yesterday with 1999 [as interpreted]. Now I would like to ask you about 1999. Do you remember in January 1999 that there was an attack on a patrol at Dulje.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was an attack not in Dulje itself, but in a place called Birac about 1 kilometre from Dulje in the direction of Prizren. A patrol set off to inspect certain areas and they described this happened on the main communication where Albanian terrorists carried out an armed attack on our police patrol on which occasion Milos Stevanovic, a colleague, was killed. Some were wounded lightly, some more gravely. These were men who were not only from Suva Reka but also from other interior Secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please get document D04-2254. I apologise, 004-2254.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Veljkovic, this is the cover page of a criminal report submitted to the Prosecutor's Office in Prizren, Suva Reka OKP [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please pull up page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report of the Suva Reka OUP in respect of the incident that we were discussing; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says there. The date is the 8th of January, 1999, and then there is also a statement of facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please show page 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We can see here a map with the place where the attack was carried out marked; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 6 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is an Official Note on a crime scene investigation in respect of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please mark this document for identification pending a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00308 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, do you recall that on the eve of the air-strikes there was an attack in Suva Reka itself, an attack or an assault on Bogdan Lazic who was a salesperson in a small newspaper stand?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know. This happened a day or two before the air-strike, or thereabouts. Around 11.00 or 12:00. He was killed at his work-place. I think that he -- I think he was a salesperson in a rubber tire store. I heard -- I had heard of this event. And this shop, this store where he worked was on the main street, the Cara Dusana Street and it was about 50 to 100 metres from the spot where Milorad Vicevic [phoen] was killed in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Veljkovic, could you tell us now, on the 26th of March, and we've established after so many years that that's when it happened, as far as you can recall, how many policemen were there in Suva Reka on that day?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the total number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, I don't mean the total number. I mean how many persons were present in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, between 10 to 15 active force policemen. And I can't really be sure about the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me help you a bit. Do you recall that there were two individuals at the duty service, one of them was the shift leader and the other one was the operator?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the assistant there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you recall that the shift leader was Gogic and that his assistant was Goran Jokic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we talked about patrols. And do you remember that there was an automobile patrol with Radovan Tanovic, Sladjan Cukaric, Miki Petkovic, and a witness who is a protected witness here, they were in this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that they went on patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is it correct that Cukaric and Tanovic were active duty police officers, whereas the other two were reservists, reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that Novkovic, Ivica was there too and that he too was a reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the driver in this automobile patrol was Ramiz Papic, one of the patrols?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the crime technician, Todor Jovanovic, was also a member of the OUP in Suva Reka at the outset -- in the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a crime technician and he worked there since 1995. He was there when I arrived. I don't know how much earlier he had started working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We also said that there were the chief of the OUP, Vitosevic; Commander Repanovic; and assistant Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 26th? Yes, in that case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, these were all the individuals who were there on that day; right? Now, do you remember that there was also, at the church bell tower, there was also a police officer?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was a command post -- an observation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- an observation post there. When I was questioned in Belgrade, I was told about this. But I don't know how the men were assigned to these observation posts. I don't know if he was there specifically or in some other place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So theses were all -- this was all the personnel who was there on the 26th in Suva Reka, can you recall if there was anyone else?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now ask you this: I'm not quite clear on what you told us about where you slept and where your office was, does this mean that both your sleeping quarters and your office were on the same premises, or were your sleeping quarters in the same area where the offices were?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sleeping quarters were at the other end of the hall in the same building. So let's say here in this area there are the sleeping quarters or the bedrooms and at the other end you have offices. This was 5 to 6 metres away, one from the other, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you actually worked in this office there and once you have completed your work, you would take this to your commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, he would give me the daily mail and then I would have to distribute the mail. And if there was a document that I needed to take to superior officers, I would do that. Or in the event that there was an extraordinary event, I would have to inform him of that and that's about it. If there was nothing, then I would just sit there. There would be no work and I would just turn on the radio and listen to the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now tell us, how many police officers were there in this building where you were in addition to yourself?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in the sleeping quarters?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean on the premises on that day on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot recall exactly, although not many people slept there. Some were on positions, deployed at positions. Some were in the hotel. So I can't really tell you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you remember on the eve of the air-strikes any measures being taken for moving the Suva Reka OUP out of those premises?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think we moved about two or three days after -- following the 26th of March. I happen to be in the duty office and I know that the colleague Jovanovic was there; he was collecting some documents. And we were supposes -- he said we are supposed to move out of here tomorrow. And this actually happened. And I don't know exactly what time it was when we moved out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But in order to move this police station, you had to undertake certain preparations. Do you recall that a few days before the war and the first two days of the war, assistant Jovanovic actually collected documents and put them on a truck that was there that was supposed to move them out?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. I would like to know this: Did every patrol that went on a mission always have protective gear, a rifle and side-arms?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, what type of uniforms did you have in 1998 and 1999? And I'm referring to the police officers of Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had dark blue uniforms. The members who were not members of the PJP. As for the PJP itself, they had light green uniforms. So you could tell us apart. But the PJP only wore those uniforms when they went on a mission, otherwise they did not wear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you talking about drab olive green camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had green and grey/blue uniforms, so I think it's about those three types of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the police officers who were regular police at Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I misunderstood you. They wore the dark blue uniform, the same uniform that I wore.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was this a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, dark blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Veljkovic, on the 26th in the morning, were you present when Commander Repanovic issued tasks according to the schedule of the work that had to be done?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would take the duty roster on the previous day and the list of patrols. He would sign this document, and I would leave it at the duty service. When -- during the working hours, the regular working hours, the shift leader who was on duty would issue these orders and the superior officers would have to sign it. Of course, the superior officer also had the authority to issue oral assignments. Whether he did or didn't on any particular day, I wouldn't know anything about that. Whether he issued an oral order which did not then -- which was not then written down in a -- on a duty roster.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember when it was that you left the -- your office and went to the OUP building on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say for sure. I know that until 7.00 p.m., when this critical event happened, when the man was murdered at the police station and the Berisha family, I cannot claim with certainty that I actually went to see Commander Repanovic or that I went to the duty office. I don't know that I left my office, and I did not hear anything about any preparations for a killing or things to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember whether in the meantime --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- whether you learned in the course of that morning that the motorised patrol had a duty, they were tasked with taking food and water to the -- to the staff personnel that was deployed around Suva Reka on that particular morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I know that this was their task every morning, not only that particular morning. So I wouldn't have anything else to add to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now pull up document -- Exhibit P269.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise it. If this is Suva Reka, I cannot really see our station here, the church. If this building in the centre of the photograph is Metohija Vino winery?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see the bus terminal?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now. Here at the end is the -- our police station and then the bus terminal. Yes, this is Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, the reason I'm asking is because you said that you could see the police station on that photograph which was D13, but I think this photograph is better than the one we saw yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually, I think the one we saw yesterday was better, but now I can find my way. I can see that this is what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you then, when you were withdrawing -- when you withdrew from Suva Reka, when you left Suva Reka, was the church and bell tower still standing?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you pin-point it; can you see it here in this photo?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that this photo was taken after June 1999? Mr. Veljkovic, did you hear me?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I thought you were addressing the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, the questions are put to you. You are the witness.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Well, we can conclude that with certainty because I believe that this was around here in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You mean where the rocks are?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, when we look at the left-hand side of this photo, we can see some houses there. Can you see the OUP building?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the OUP building at the end here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which one is it? Could you please mark it with an X.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will. I'll do that. Here. I've put an X on the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. So the building marked with X is the OUP building. Now, tell us, please, can you see the building where your sleeping quarters were?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you please put the number 1 on that building?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here it is. I'll put number 1 on the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now please mark with a number 3 the place where you were when you went out onto the street. Now, is this the main street, the Prizren-Pristina Road, so-called Cara Dusana Street?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So you want me to mark the spot from which I observed people fleeing? Is that what you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you were standing there. Now, could you, please, just put number 3 to mark the road that is Restanski Put so that we know which is which.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now could you please mark the main road with a dash and an arrow to show the direction Pristina-Prizren, the way the road runs.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to put an arrow and what number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, tell us, please, where was the bell tower before it was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bell tower was next to this building here. You see this tree and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you please put a dot, a number 5, to mark that spot.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I'll do it. It was about here in this area, roughly speaking. I think it's probably a bit to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you this: I can see a portion of Restanski Put -- or rather, let's do it this way: Tell me, did you see your colleagues, the policemen, who had left before you in the direction of the Berisha houses? Did you see them at all?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really say with certainty that I did see when they left. However, when I entered the duty service office and from this office --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That was not actually my question. Can you -- let's try this way. Can you mark the Berisha house with a number 6.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that you did not know at the time that that was their last name, but do you know whether there were any other houses belonging to the Berisha family or was this the only one?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know about this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please listen carefully and answer my next question. When you came out of the police station and after the group of your work-mates left some minutes before you, when you arrived in the place number 2, did you see them as you were standing there? Did you see your colleagues, policemen?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what did you see in that place?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At place number 2 I heard automatic rifle shots and I saw people running from the courtyard towards the bus station and the shopping centre. As I said already, some were killed there and the rest ran off trying to find shelter in one of the shops on the bus station compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the courtyard you saw them run out of; if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mark it nicely, please. Can you mark the spot at which you saw the people as they were running?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll put a short line.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you also put an arrow to show the direction in which they ran?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is. They were running towards the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you place a number 7 next to the arrow.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, you say you did not see the policemen but you heard the gun-shots. Could you see in which direction they were shooting?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you went outside and reached the place number 2, did you see some of the bodies on Restanski Put?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything with any certainty. This was within a span of a few seconds. I can't tell you exactly whether by the time I arrived at the place number 2 there had already been dead people there; but in a matter of a few seconds perhaps, following that, I saw them fall dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. Had they been lying on the ground dead by the time you arrived, or did you see them fall?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you with certainty is that within the first few seconds of my arrival, I heard the shots and saw them fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Restanski Put Street, as we refer to it in jargon, is it the -- is it Miladin Popovic Street?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think Miladin Popovic Street is the first intersection with Restanski Put to the left. It's a rather short street of about 100 metres. It is next to the Metohija Vino company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, we see a good stretch of Restanski Put here. As you moved along that street, did you go further up the street to the part which we don't see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, but I'm not certain. I don't know exactly where we made the U-turn and went back to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you see those people fleeing, as you saw them, where were they running to?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They crossed Restanski Put running towards the bus station compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate where they crossed the street?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put the arrow number 7 there, and then in the direction of the building with the green roof. I think they found a passage in between because there was a flight of stairs there, and they passed by the news stand or some kiosks for fast food that were there. They passed next to them. But this is all within the bus station compound or yard. And then they continued onwards towards the shopping centre. I no longer saw them at that point in time, but I presume that they wanted to shelter in one of the shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where did you lose sight of them?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say precisely that I saw them -- that I did not see them anymore, but I can tell you approximately. Do you want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, where the line is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you place a number 8 there.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Once they reached that point, you no longer knew where they were going, it was only your assumption?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about that point in time.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, were there any policemen in the part around the Metohija Vino company and -- where those people were running? Did you see any policemen there?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a position, a police position at the Metohija Vino company, but I don't know whether they were at the location number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see them there?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As you were standing in the place number 2, did you see any policemen anywhere?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, what followed? You saw them fleeing, you heard the shots without seeing a single policemen; what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also cannot tell you anything with certainty, but I think I returned either to the entrance of the police station or I went to the duty officers' room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In this area, save for the civilians, did you see a single VJ soldier there?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see a single tank, a self-propelled vehicle, or any military equipment?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see on that day, the 26th, any members of any other unit save for the police unit in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see any trucks parked in front of the police station, two trucks used to transport the policemen?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you set out, although you said you don't know where you went to, you did mention the police station, who did you find in the OUP building in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything with any certainty. I know that the officers were there, our superiors, that is to say, the commander, his assistant, and the chief. As for the policemen, I was there with the two reservists because later on we started loading the bodies. I can't tell you who the shift leader was in the duty office. There must have been someone, but I no longer remember who was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was the assistant supposed to be in the duty office on communication lines?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the assistant to the commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, the assistant shift leader.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There must have been someone there, but I no longer remember who was the shift leader or his assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember or did you hear anyone get in touch over the radio saying that a patrol came under attack and that they needed assistance?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that; therefore, I cannot say with any certainty whether there was an attack or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear the commander issue a task to check certain locations and find locators or markers used to guide NATO planes?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Save for your part of work, did you participate in any regular police tasks in the police station in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that on that day you were not a duty officer?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify one thing which remains unclear to me. You reached a certain point along Restanski Put and made a U-turn; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that following the truck, you did not enter the police station, but rather you turned towards the crafts and trades centre?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are quite right. I turned towards that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since we see part of the streets here, did you follow the streets or did you use a shortcut since you were on foot?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I followed the truck on foot together with the two reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you come out on to Cara Dusana Street and turn right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First to the left; and then as we were coming back, to the right. We went this way, picked up those, and then back, and then right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So we are already at the point in time as you were going back. From the street you turned ...

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Following the truck, how did you reach the small business centre or trades and crafts centre?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On foot. Yesterday I marked the building where the Berisha family members were killed. It is next to the gas station where I'm pointing more or less. It is perhaps 5 or 6 metres away from Cara Dusana Street. I think it is one of the buildings of the small businesses centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you followed the truck all along reaching the building that you, yesterday, marked?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you mark it again. Can you put a number 9 there.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The building across the street, across the number 9 and to the left, what building is that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the municipal hall where the Territorial Defence had its offices. I think that's the yellow building, the first one. Next to it was the municipal misdemeanours office or court, and next to it was the post office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the municipal hall.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of the two buildings, I'm not certain which one it is. I'm not certain. I think it's the one in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was there a kiosk nearby?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there was one just in front of the building number 9. Perhaps 2 metres from the street on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see a shop nearby that sold liquor, or a bar?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across from number 9, in this group of buildings, there was a set of shops held by Albanians. There were several owners. They were taxpayers individually. And the first building was a shop. The second building was another shop. And there was another with a catering establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the truck enter the part where the shops were that you just described?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The truck could only move along the main street and the street further down. Although, when the shops received supplies, the trucks would park there to unload the goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you reached the shop, who was there of your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Number 9.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you with certainty that the reservist Miroslav Petkovic was there, as well as the professional policemen Radovan Tanovic and Sladjan Cukaric. After that, the people from the municipal utility company came and the undertakers, they were, for the most part, between 13 and 15 years of age. I don't know for sure whether Boban, the doctor, was already there or whether he arrived later. In any case, I know for sure that he wore a military Territorial Defence uniform that was green and he had an automatic rifle. I can say that with certainty. As for the other colleagues who were there, I cannot tell you anything more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While on the topic of the Territorial Defence it was already the time when the war had begun; am I right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the TO members were issued with their own weapons?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Dr. Boban was employed at the health clinic in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the manager of the clinic. The general opinion was that he was a good professional in what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was a Soko [phoen] officer from the Suva Reka police station Jovan -- Todor Jovanovic there?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As you were moving along the street, did you see anyone at the gas station?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that you followed the truck?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who was in the truck?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, the driver was there, but there's no way for me to recognise him any longer. I don't know whether he was from Suva Reka or Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you exclude the possibility that that truck belonged to the public utilities company in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You followed the truck therefore?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where did the truck stop and who stopped it?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot make out what you are asking me, but you are probably asking me about the point where it stopped to have the bodies loaded. It stopped at the place number 9 because there was a space there for it to stop between the Metohija Vino company and the small businesses centre. This was a rather large area. It stopped so that the cabin of the truck was facing the municipal hall, and the trailer was already opened. It was parked in such a way that it could turn either left or right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Why did you follow the truck on foot along Cara Dusana Street?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because none of the work-mates who were with me wanted to get in the truck. Therefore, I didn't either.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's clear. And you wouldn't all fit in anyhow. But once you reach the intersection, why didn't you go to the police station? Why did you continue following it?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I continued following it because as we were loading the bodies, I heard some shots from the direction of the municipal building. I supposed that the Berisha family members hid in a shop and that our men found them easily, and they simply started killing them. That is why I went there because I knew that the corpses should not be left just like that. This was a great deal of bodies, and there would have been an outbreak if we had left them. If we had left them, there would be many more accused and people prosecuted than there already were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, could you please just tell us the facts that you knew on the 26th, on that very day, and not the things that you learned later on. So my question is where were you when you heard, you said you heard a blast of an explosion, where were you when that happened?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on Restanski Road but where exactly, I can't pin-point the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I know that was what you said yesterday, that you couldn't remember, but from that place where you were, you could not see the small businesses centre, could you?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see the small business centre from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you see what was going on inside the small business centre or shopping centre?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't see exactly the place where the killing was taking place. I heard the shots, but I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When did you learn for the first time that these people were hiding somewhere?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw them fleeing, I assumed, that was what occurred to me at that moment, that they were returning in order to hide somewhere. So this was just my assumption. I couldn't go and see where exactly they were hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I totally agree with you, but that's why I'm asking you. I need to know what you knew at that time because, you see, you marked this number 9 and in fact, they could have gone to the municipal building or the post office building, or they could go, this is an open area, so they could go further. And as far as I know, there was another Berisha settlement behind those buildings?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right then. What about the first part of my question?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really add anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you heard the blast, the explosion, you didn't know where they were, you didn't know the location?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And from the spot where you were, you could not see these buildings marked with number 9; right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not see it, but I could hear the blasts and I knew that it must be approximately in the area of this shopping centre or the small business centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. But how then did you know that you should go to this building marked with number 9?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I returned from Restanski Road, at the spot where I marked with number 4, I saw that -- where the petrol station was on the road or on the sidewalk, I saw a police officer there, or actually, I saw some men. I'm not sure exactly who they were. And I assumed that some people must have been killed in one of those small businesses. And then when I came up, when I came closer, I saw exactly the spot where these people had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who was with you when you reached the building marked with number 9?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got there with two reserve officers and the truck driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So they were with you all along?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And about Novkovic, you said that he wasn't doing anything, he was just going, walking behind you?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. He was not loading the bodies. It would be sinful if I were to say that he was shooting at these men, he wasn't. He wasn't doing anything. He just felt sick. He could not bring himself to loading these bodies. He just didn't want to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, tell me, as you walked along Restanski Put, did you make any detours?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can I conclude then that you did not go around the building marked number 6, along that alley and behind the building?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You told us that before you began loading the bodies onto the truck you went to get a rifle?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where was your rifle?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My automatic rifle was in the administration office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You also had a pistol; right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me then, what did you need a rifle for if you were going to load those bodies?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way, this Restanski Put Road was very risky and dangerous. There were terrorists and they could come out at any moment and shoot at us. So I needed it for self-defence, that's the only reason. Because it was wartime and that's how it was. Although, there were a lot of people who got killed on Restanski Put, there were land-mines there sometimes, people would run onto them, and then there were other incidents. Zoran Randelovic or Randenovic, he was the chief of the Aleksinac OUP, he was killed there. I think the driver who was driving him was also killed there. AND that was the reason why I took the rifle with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have a cartridge belt on your rifle?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had the rifle issued, but I did not have a cartridge belt. Although, in such situations you wouldn't even take it with you, you would take it off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, yesterday you told us that at one point you entered this pizzeria and that one person, I think a woman, moved and this startled you and you fled?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was woman who was lying next to the door. And when I was questioned the first time, there were questions to the effect, and the first -- one of the questions was what did the woman who was wounded and sitting by the door, what did she say to you. And then I told them, as I mentioned it yesterday, I said that I had left the rifle by the door and -- because it was interfering with my loading of the bodies. And then when I left -- when I put this rifle and put it by the door, then she addressed me and I was so startled, I got frightened and I left. Although, that is one of the typical errors that policemen do when they assume that someone is dead whereas they are actually alive, and that's how you can get killed. If a man was to be in that position lying down as pretending to be dead and then being in fact alive, then they could use their weapon once you turned your back and shoot at you, and then this would be trouble. But this was a woman, so I left the room frightened, although, I felt frightened even before that, because this was a horrible event. This was something that is terrible to even think about let alone talk about. And I said then, This woman is alive. And then one of my colleagues entered the room and fired a bullet and the woman was killed. Although she had only been wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but what was it, what was the cause of your fear? Were you afraid that she might shoot at you?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that point it just occurred to me that she might have a weapon maybe with her. You couldn't know. She might want to shoot even though she would be killed herself in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, was it common for civilians to be armed and to actually open fire on police officers in those days?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, citizens of Albanian ethnicity in 1998, for them this was normal. It was absolutely -- it was quite normal to fire a bullet at a policeman or a Serb, just a Serb national. This was something that was very easy for them to do. And for most citizens of Albanian ethnicity, this was just a normal occurrence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Tell us now, do you remember that during the war and even before the war, that members of the KLA after they went on a mission, they would change their clothes and put on civilian clothes so that in this way they would escape detection?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You never participated in such an action?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever take part in road checks and checks for -- searches for weapons and things like that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this did happen. I did do that before the war. In 1994, when I was appointed to Suva Reka, from that point on, most people had dealings with persons who had weapons, unauthorised weapons, automatic rifles, pistols, and so on. So these people would be brought to the police station, interviewed, and some of them would be summoned to come to the police station as suspects, others not. I don't know exactly what the procedure was, but I know that whenever there was a suspicion that someone might own a fire-arm, they would bring them in to check the weapons. Sometimes they would have a weapon, they would be brought into the police station, and then -- and of course, they would possess an unauthorised weapon, and then after this interview they would bring another weapon in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, do you know of instances where Albanians would voluntarily surrender their arms because they knew that there would be amnesty? Do you know of such instance that they would come in voluntarily and surrender their weapon?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that. I know that we received a telegram from the ministry. And on one occasion, I don't recall how it worked, but on the second occasion they were given a two-month period - and this did not only refer to Kosovo but for the entire territory of Serbia - that whoever had unauthorised weapons could come and surrender them and they would not be amnestied, they would not be submitted to criminal prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me, other than the truck that you were following, did you see any other trucks on the 26th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that with certainty. I cannot claim either way, that there was or wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you set off from the spot you marked on number 2 and you headed up Restanski Put Road; correct? Could you tell us now, please, where did you find the bodies that you said you loaded onto the truck, what spot was that at?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the spot marked with number 7 and where the arrow is. Where the arrow is, actually, below the 7, that's where we found the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So as you were walking along that road, you did not find any other bodies along the road?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that I didn't. If somebody else said that they did, they can explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I agree. Now, you said that you walked about a kilometre, a kilometre and a half, and that that lasted about 15 minutes or so?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then conclude that the shots could only be heard by those individuals who had left the police station before you?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you recall that those persons were Cukaric, Tanovic, and Miki Petkovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to explore this. You said that throughout this there was witness, whose name we don't want to mention, with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he was a member of the patrol on that day?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we set off, he was in the courtyard of the police station. I can't remember what duty he was assigned to on that particular day, and I cannot remember what he had done up until that point. As for the rest, I've explained how it transpired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And the other three, Cukaric, Tanovic, and Petkovic, were they on the patrol roster for that day, as far as you know? Were they members of the patrol?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say with certainty. I know that they were frequently on patrol. Whether Radovan Tanovic was there, whether he had been at his home the previous day and then his unit left, I know he was a member of the special unit. But -- so they couldn't take him. He could not go to the positions where his unit had gone to subsequently, so he remained there at the station. And I know that he was there and these other police members, I know that the driver was also a member of the patrol, our colleague, Ramiz Papic. But whether it was on that particular day or whether he had some other assignment on that day, I can't say that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I correct if I say that there were two patrols a day and that they would take turns?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we actually had three shifts -- three patrol shifts a day. Until the attacks began, we had two shift patrols per day; but when the war broke out, that changed and we had three shifts a day. So those shifts were 8 hours-1600; then 1600-2400; and then 2400-0800. Now, who was on those patrol, I couldn't really say that. Well, the person, for instance, who worked from 8.00 to 4.00, 8.00 to 1600 today, then in the evening they would work from 8.00 to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is that how it was throughout the war, that there were three shifts of patrols?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, throughout the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the people who had left the station are the people you found at the location number 9?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The person whose name we don't want to mention, why would he have a reason to say that he was a member of the patrol and that he was with the three other men rather than with you?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe on that day he was a member of the vehicle patrol, under the schedule. I cannot say anything with certainty. The computer that I kept, which is now in Krusevac, if it's still there, can be used to check that. They should look into the roster and orders for the 26th of March, 1999, and they will see exactly whether he was a member of the patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Veljkovic, I'm asking you about your knowledge concerning such evidence that can be obtained, I presume. But I'm interested in your knowledge. That person told us that he was a member of the vehicle patrol and that he was between the buildings where the number 6 is, and then that he went to the building number 9 and that he did not work at all on the loading of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat, I'm not certain what were his tasks that day, and whether anything changed in the course of his shift. As for what he said, that he was not with me, I told him in Belgrade that he was and then he fell silent. I may be wrong, but I think his story is to his detriment. Therefore, I stand by what I said. And that is that as of the beginning and until the end, we were loading the bodies together. As for any period preceding that, between 8.00 and noon and later in the afternoon, I can't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to give this unmarked hard copy to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is it, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to put him the part of the statement given in 2004 to an investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is his own statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please turn --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for clarification, is that the transcript of the audio recording of his interview or is it a statement that was taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stamp, this is what you gave me and what you used yesterday. You have the same copy as well as the court in Belgrade. I only provided the witness with the document you used yesterday. It is K040 page 85 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Djurdjic repeat the number of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, did you find the page 63?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you read out the bottom part of the page?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Did you see a reserve policemen ..." I don't want to read the first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, first I wanted to tell the Chamber and Mr. Stamp that it is page 16 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Investigative judge: "Did you see a reserve policemen?" Witness Veljkovic: "He was there." Judge: "Where was he?" Witness: "He was in front of the cafe bar. I don't think he killed anyone. I can't say he did. He may have or he may have not."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please turn the next page and read out the first two questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judge: "You didn't see him?" Witness: "He was there but I didn't see him kill anyone."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is your statement. The first statement before a court following the statement you gave to the police?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the second statement. The first one was in 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But this one was the first before a court?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you this. In this statement you say that you saw the witness in front of the building number 9 and that he did not shoot, that he was merely there?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably mixed things up. I believe I got confused. I can tell you that this person was with me as of the moment we started loading those bodies. He was on Restanski Put when we went up and returned next to the building number 9. I think the two of us loaded most of the bodies. After that, we received help from the people of the public utilities company. I think that reservist left this place at the number 9 building shortly before me. Then I returned to the station. Although, not all the bodies had been loaded by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that none of the three of you on that day fired either a rifle or a side-arm?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you about me with certainty. As for the other two colleagues, I didn't see them fire. If anyone else did, then that person should explain. And still, they may have been firing in the air. It's not the same as firing on people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You are saying to us that you did not see the two colleagues fire?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Throughout the time they were with you?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you drink any alcohol with the witness, whose name we don't want to mention, on that day when you were next to the building number 9?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know I did not. I do take a drink here and there, but I don't get drunk. Secondly, the situation was such that there was no time to have any alcohol that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the other policemen in front of the building number 9, did you see them consume alcohol?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that with any certainty. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You left before the end of the loading of bodies. You returned to the police station?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you did not see the truck leave?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You don't know in what direction it left?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could presume that it would not have been an ordinary thing to take the corpses towards Pristina because that road was under attack. I believe the truck went towards Prizren. When I was being questioned by the authorities, then I did tell them that the corpses were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On the 26th, you did not know where the truck left to?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe it is our time for the technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, we spent 35 or 40 minutes marking this aerial photo again. Did you want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I do. I seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D00309, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, on the 26th of March, 1999, did you see Milorad Nisevic as you went along Restanski Put or by the pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know Zoran Petkovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I only knew his brother Miroslav, not him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that Zoran Petkovic was not a member of the reserve police force in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How should I ask you this without sounding silly, but in any case, on that occasion, did you see anyone firing whom you did not know?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right, Mr. Veljkovic, in saying that Milan Cifka [phoen] was not an OUP Suva Reka employee in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the village of Ranic [phoen] in 1998 and 1999 there was no police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have document D004-2262.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see the first page of the document?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Have a close look.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we next move to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, does this schematic reflect the layout of the building on the ground floor and the first floor of the police station in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you were shown this during the trial before the war crimes Chamber in Belgrade; do you recall it?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shown schematics, but I don't recall this one in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We said that this is the layout of the building, and that it is correct?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljkovic, this is the ground floor; right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We see the entrance door to the ground floor. Can you mark that with a 1.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it says the small room?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Wherever you think is the entrance, mark the entrance with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please mark the entrance to the duty office.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to mark it with a 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the entrance.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the duty office is to the right?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with a 2.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this where the shift leader of the duty office sits?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about communications, where is that equipment, can you mark it with a 3.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next mark the detention room with a 4.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Veljkovic, when one is in the duty office, where would the courtyard be?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the courtyard is to the right of the number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please put a dash, a line there, and mark it with a 5.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where were you when you heard Commander Repanovic say to the policemen to go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And to me, and I refused, is this what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in two things. Were you with them there or did they leave first and were you told to join them, and where did it all take place?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were supposed to leave, and I came at that point, having heard what commander Repanovic told me, I refused. I can tell you where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you present when he told them what to do?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, show me where you were.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point -- how do you want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: First tell me where were you so as to make sure you were in the building or maybe outside.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it says the duty officers' room, I was just in front of that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mark it with an X.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And put a 6 there.

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you were in front of the building where you arrived?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you arrived, where were the other policemen?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right of the number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How far?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 3 to 4 metres from the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were they doing as you came?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply saw them armed and that they were getting ready to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Veljkovic, members of the vehicle patrol are always armed and equipped when out on a mission or a task?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was it something extraordinary to see them dressed like that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not given the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As you were approaching, were they leaving or doing something else?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they went to the right of this number 6 towards the carpool because that's where the parking area was for the vehicles. Approximately there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So they went around the corner; correct? When you came to the spot marked with number 6, is that where the commander of the police station was?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was there. Maybe a metre or two to the left or right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you are telling us that you can't remember what he told you then?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no way I can remember what he told me, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But you concluded that you didn't want to go?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I simply decided that I did not want to go anywhere with these men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I went inside, I entered the hallway on the ground floor, and -- to the right where the duty service office is, and I think that I sat down there by the door, by the very door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Veljkovic, now, tell us please, what did the commander do once you entered the office of the duty service?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not say another word to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where he went?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether he remained in the yard where I put the number 6, or whether he left -- went to his own office. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, from the point when you entered the office of the duty service onwards, did you see him for the remainder of the day?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned from the building and the loading of the bodies was still going on, he was in the building. I did see him. But what he did, that's really his business.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you talk to him at all after that?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nor did he address me in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, so we are at the point in time where you are in the duty service office. What happens next?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what happens is what I told you already. The room, the detention room, the patrol brought a man, an Albanian to the detention room. He was a suspect because the patrol found him shooting at the police. So this was an armed attack on the police. He was held in detention there. When I came there, a few days before when he was brought there, I heard sounds, I was in the hallway, I heard sounds from the detention room. I asked what it was, what was going on, and I was told that he had been brought there. However, I'm not sure about the rest. We know what the procedure is when there is a suspect brought in as a suspect. There is a fixed procedure that has to be followed when that happens. Whether they actually complied with the procedure or not, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come back to this. But I would like to know this: It says here "Detention Unit." However, the Suva Reka OUP did not have a room that was a detention room. It was, rather, a -- it was actually a room where a person was kept until they were sent to a Detention Unit or to the jail?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this room that was used for detaining persons was a problem everywhere, and the same is true of Suva Reka. This room, in my view, and maybe I'm not right, was not suitable for detaining people there, for a person staying in that room. At least not according to our rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I wanted to ask you about. You said that some person was held in that room for a number of days. Could you tell us, in regard to the 26th of March, when was this man brought there?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he might have been brought the 23rd or the 24th of March there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that the war had not started yet on the 23rd or 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that on the 24th in the evening, the state of war was declared? It was only then that it was declared?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So in peacetime, the Suva Reka OUP did not have a crime inspector who dealt with terrorism, who investigated terrorism?

utterances.speaker: VELIBOR VELJKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not. I'm not sure, and I cannot say for certain either way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
